newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips end up on rebound in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips end up on rebound in quiet trade.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip stocks closed up on a technical rebound from Friday's sharp drop, but trading remained quiet, dealers said.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed up 12.04 points to 1,203.36, and the all-share EMAS index closed up 2.60 to 338.98.
"There has been no serious buying," said a dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage house.
"There were certainly some bargains in the market this morning," said Dominic Armstrong, head of research at Pesaka Jardine Fleming.
At the close, around 175 million shares were traded, valued at 1.18 billion ringgit. Losers outpaced gainers 323 to 265, with 149 stocks remaining unchanged.
United Engineers was up 80 cents to 22.70 ringgit. Analysts said the opening of a new highway would provide earnings from toll collections from January.
Proton was up 30 to 15.40, after having dropped 80 cents on Friday. "It has plenty of upside at these levels," said the head of research of a foreign brokerage house in Kuala Lumpur.
Newly-listed Industrial Concrete closed at 5.80 ringgit, after debuting at 4.70 on an offer price of 3.00 ringgit.
